There are quite a few people who enjoy the game and want to play it but lack the skill, so they spend money to boost their characters' power; however, they are now quitting because inflation has made even that approach too difficult to sustain.

Doesn't that make sense? They find the game fun but challenging, so they spend money to strengthen their characters. After all, if they had wanted a difficult gameplay experience, they wouldn't have needed to make their characters powerful in the first place.

It is truly disheartening to watch them leave. A player base that spends money is essential for the game to keep running, so their departure makes it difficult to sustain the game. My proposal regarding ECogs: 

**Make the first 5 revives cost 1 Ecog each. Afterwards they can cost 3 Ecogs. **

One issue with each revive costing 3 Ecogs is that while you can *technically* use ~5 free revives per DTide, trying to do so forces you to do your DTide runs over several sessions across the entire 14 day rotation as opposed to doing them at your own pace.

Changing it so the first 5 revives per rotation cost only 1 Ecog makes it so you can do your DTide runs at your preferred pace without losing out on revives (I think punishing people who can’t or don’t want to do DTide runs over several days is just mean). 

This *would* increase the free revives per rotation from 5 to 8, but I see the 3 extra revives as a bonus reward for those who are dedicated enough to work for it.
